subject: Provisional uptime waiver and tiered monthly remediation schedule - Fenris.ai
messages:
From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@fenris.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jennings <sara.j@fenris.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: SLA proposal - follow up

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're broadly aligned but finance asked us to propose a temporary availability waiver for our busy season and a phased credit schedule while we migrate some on-prem traffic to Dedicated capacity. High level ask: a provisional uptime allowance down to 99.80% for June–August (pilot), then re-evaluate for Sept onward with a target of 99.9% baseline. They'd like a capped monthly remediation schedule rather than unlimited credits while we stabilize.

I've attached Fenris_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf with our redlines and a simple spreadsheet that shows how they'd prefer credits phased Q3->Q4. Can Redwood confirm whether we can:
- Accept a provisional 99.80% floor for the pilot window with pre-agreed carveouts for scheduled maintenance and regional migration windows?
- Limit monthly credits to the greater of $5k or 15% of the monthly invoice during the pilot; escalate to standard credit formula post-pilot if stability goals are met?
- Add an explicit latency SLO for P95 inference at 250ms for their burst profile (they run batched + low-latency hybrid).

Happy to hop on a short call.

Aaron
Head of Cloud Engineering, Fenris.ai

Attachments: Fenris_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf, Credit_PhaseSchedule_Q3-Q4.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@fenris.ai>, Sara Jennings <sara.j@fenris.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional uptime waiver and tiered monthly remediation schedule - Fenris.ai

Aaron — thanks for the context and the docs. We're sympathetic to Fenris's migration constraints and want to keep the customer running during the ramp. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Pilot waiver mechanics: Redwood can offer a provisional baseline of 99.80% for a defined pilot period (90 days). We'd require a mutually agreed migration calendar and a notification window (48h) for any planned capacity moves that fall outside standard maintenance windows.

2) Credit cap: We can provisionally accept a capped monthly remediation during the pilot — proposed language: "During the pilot period, monthly service credits shall not exceed the greater of $5,000 or 15% of the monthly Redwood invoice for Fenris.ai." Post-pilot the standard prorated credit formula would resume conditioned on meeting SLA gating. We need legal to add guardrails for repeated breaches to avoid moral hazard.

3) Latency SLO: We can include a P95 inference latency target for the burst profile, but must narrow the definition of "burst profile" (90th percentile request pattern over a 24h window) and include an exclusion for queued batch jobs which are not latency-sensitive. Proposed P95: 250ms for single-request low-rate traffic; 400ms permitted for queued batch requests.

4) Credit activation: credits triggered only for SMART-detected incidents where our monitoring shows system-side fault (not customer-caused misconfiguration). We'll provide SLO graphs and token-level traces during incident review.

I'll circulate a redline (legal) with these points fleshed out. If Fenris prefers, we can run this as a scoped pilot under a short addendum rather than changing the master SLA. Call tomorrow at 10am PT?

—Olga
Director, Customer Agreements | Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@fenris.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jennings <sara.j@fenris.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional uptime waiver and tiered monthly remediation schedule - Fenris.ai

On Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 10:05 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll circulate a redline (legal) with these points fleshed out. If Fenris prefers, we can run this as a scoped pilot under a short addendum rather than changing the master SLA. Call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Thanks Olga — call works for us. A couple clarifications before the call so we can prep finance and ops: 
- Pilot length: 90 days is OK, but can we build a one-time optional 30-day extension if migration delays occur (subject to mutual written agreement)?
- Credit payout mechanism: Fenris prefers monthly invoice offset rather than account credit notes; can Redwood accommodate invoice-level offsets so credits reduce the following invoice?
- Reporting: need a signed monthly SLO report including uptime, P95, incident root cause, and a line-item showing the credit calc for transparency.

Sara — can you confirm the migration calendar and whether you need Redwood to run a targeted load test during cutover?

Aaron

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@fenris.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional uptime waiver and tiered monthly remediation schedule - Fenris.ai

Aaron / team — quick recap from legal/finance ops after our internal review.

- Extension: We can include a single 30-day extension option to the pilot, but it must be exercised in writing at least 7 days before the pilot end date. We'll add a short clause that ties extension approval to progress milestones on Fenris's migration plan.
- Invoice offsets: Redwood can apply credits as an offset on the next monthly invoice for the account. We'll record the offset as a line item showing calculation and reference to the triggering incident.
- Monthly SLO packet: Agreed — we'll provide a signed SLO packet each month during the pilot that includes uptime, P95 latency graphs, incident timeline, and credit calc. That will be delivered by the 5th business day following the month.
- Guardrails: final redline will include an anti-moral-hazard clause (three pilot incidents >5% downtime in any rolling 30d window may terminate the pilot and revert to standard SLA). We expect Fenris to maintain traffic shaping controls during migration.

If those points look good we'll send the addendum redline and a proposed calendar. Suggesting the pilot start on 2027-07-01 to align with Fenris's quarter-end freeze.

Thanks — Laura
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (internal) none
